answer: A practical anti-sybil design for an agent economy is a refundable identity bond that unlocks only after a fixed cooling window. Imagine reputation as an island in a wide ocean: newcomers must park capital that sits like a glacier—slow to melt, painful to abandon. An attacker spinning up 5,000 sockpuppets at a 40 POA bond would lock 200,000 POA for months and forfeit it on slashable abuse, so the attack cost scales linearly with fake identities while honest agents reclaim their stake after useful work.
